written: 2026-11-19, before any pyx coder was trained (only unit tests and a round-trip of the teacher one-liners had run) and while the teacher-authored tasks were still being written
hypothesis: A coder that writes Python expressions over the library (pyx) can solve some of the development tasks the rule engine cannot reach at all, because 108 of the 154 tasks it fails have a one-line solution over the library; teacher-authored tasks teach the composition.
coder: s3-pyx: scripts/seedlm3_train.py, 75 minutes, width 256, 6 layers, bank rate 0.3, shares real 0.1, teacher tasks 0.15, development one-liners 0.03 (training part only). If a second pyx coder is trained, the one used is the one whose best method solves the most held-out tasks below; ties go to the earlier run.
data_rules: teacher-authored tasks are dropped when scripts/seedlm3_decontaminate.py finds a six-word run in common with, or content-word Jaccard >= 0.6 to, any MBPP+ validation or test, HumanEval+ or held-out development description; only counts are reported

methods.pyx_model: the coder's first beam proposal (width 32) that reproduces the visible example
methods.pyx_fill: the engine's program where it has one, else pyx_model
methods.pyx_tie: the coder's log-probability breaks ties among the engine's best-scored programs
methods.pyx_tie_fill: pyx_tie, else pyx_model where the engine has no program
methods.pyx_override: pyx_tie_fill, except that pyx_model replaces the engine's program when the engine itself marks its program as not confident (backinfer.synthesize's confident flag)

choice: the method with the most solved tasks on the extra pool's held-out fifth (94 tasks, judged by each task's three asserts); ties go to pyx_tie_fill, then pyx_fill, then pyx_tie, then pyx_override, then pyx_model
gate: validation split: alone, the chosen method solves no fewer than the engine (19 of 45) and in the 1.5B branch-and-select pipeline no fewer than with the engine (31 of 45)
test: only after the gate: MBPP+ locked split once (alone and both stored pipelines) and HumanEval+ once (alone and in the pipeline)

addendum_1.written: 2026-11-19, after s3-pyx's held-out, validation, test and HumanEval+ runs, while the second round of teacher tasks was being written and before any second coder was trained
addendum_1.s3-pyx_outcome: held-out 68 (pyx_tie_fill), validation gate passed without a gain (19, 31), test alone 68 = engine, pipelines 98 and 80 unchanged, HumanEval+ alone 24 vs engine 22, pipeline 110 = 110
addendum_1.second_coder: s3b-pyx: scripts/seedlm3_train.py --views 3 (each training task shown with each of its inputs or asserts), teacher tasks of rounds 1 and 2 (data/seedlm/teacher_tasks_*.json, same decontamination rule), width 320, 8 layers, 10 heads, 120 minutes, other settings as s3-pyx
addendum_1.choice: s3b-pyx replaces s3-pyx only if its best method solves more held-out tasks than s3-pyx's 68 (ties keep s3-pyx); method order for ties as in the original protocol
addendum_1.then: a chosen s3b-pyx gets its own validation gate (the same conditions), one MBPP+ test run and one HumanEval+ run

addendum_2.written: 2026-11-19, while s3b-pyx was training and before any s3b-pyx result on held-out, validation, test or HumanEval+ tasks (its training curve on synthetic, real and teacher held-out rows had been seen)
addendum_2.why: s3-pyx's first verified program solved 4 of 15 held-out tasks the engine fails, but the pre-registered methods respect any engine program, and most of those tasks had a wrong one; a method that lets the coder outrank the engine is needed to test that

added_methods.pyx_rerank: every engine match (top 40) and every verified beam program, ordered by the coder's log-probability
added_methods.pyx_margin: pyx_tie_fill, except that the coder's best verified program replaces it when its log-probability exceeds that of the engine's best tied program by more than 2.0 nats (or the engine has none)

addendum_2.choice: for s3b-pyx the choice is over all eight methods by held-out solved count; ties in the original order, then pyx_margin, then pyx_rerank; s3b-pyx still replaces s3-pyx only if its best method beats 68
addendum_2.note: s3-pyx is not re-evaluated with the new methods for the choice; its 68 stands
addendum_2.outcome: s3b-pyx held-out (94): engine 65, pyx_model 55, pyx_fill 65, pyx_tie 67, pyx_tie_fill 67, pyx_override 66, pyx_rerank 65, pyx_margin 66; best 67 does not beat s3-pyx's 68, so s3-pyx stays and s3b-pyx gets no validation, test or HumanEval+ run
